title: The Woman Who Humoured Her Lover At Her Husband's Expense

full_text:
In the market town of Tripoli lived a merchant named Khalid, known for his gentle demeanor and quiet habits. An idle young aristocrat of the town, foolishly assuming Khalid was simple-minded, tried to ingratiate himself with Khalid's household through extravagant flatteries and secret messages.

Khalid, whose quiet exterior concealed a mind like a polished razor, intercepted the youth's letters.
Instead of flying into a useless rage, Khalid decided to teach the interloper an unforgettable lesson in public embarrassment.

Khalid composed a reply in an anonymous hand, inviting the young gallant to climb the orchard wall at midnight to receive 'the golden chest of the family heirlooms'.
The youth, dressed in his finest embroidered silk coat and perfumed with musk, scaled the garden wall with an empty velvet sack, dreaming of easy riches.

As he dropped onto the orchard grass, he found himself surrounded not by treasure, but by three large, wooden bee-hives that Khalid had strategically arranged beneath the trellis!
Before the youth could move, Khalid, standing safely behind a protective mesh on the terrace, lightly shook the hives with a cord.

A cloud of angry midnight bees swarmed out!
The terrified young aristocrat ran blindly through the briars, shedding his silk coat, losing his slippers, and jumping straight into the muddy irrigation ditch, where he croaked like a bullfrog among the reeds!

The next morning, Khalid brought the muddy silk coat and slippers to the town market square, offering them to the highest bidder as 'the lost attire of a midnight gardener'.
The entire town recognized the youth's coat, and the young boaster was so thoroughly laughed at that he fled Tripoli for a year.

Khalid returned home to his garden, demonstrating that quiet prudence and clever defensive wit are more than enough to protect domestic honor from foolish arrogance.
moral: Underestimating the quiet wisdom of a faithful partner leads to the swift exposure of duplicity.
